details:
Hello VRChat Team,

I’m the owner of Night Life, a VRChat/resonite-based community focused on social interaction and immersive world-building. I’m writing to formally request a Terms of Service update focused on the handling of adult and sexual content, along with the implementation of an NSFW warning system similar to Reddit’s.

🔄 Requested Changes & Additions

1. 🔐 Clarity in ToS: Adult/Sexual Content

The current ToS around sexual content is too vague, which leads to inconsistent enforcement and confusion. I propose:

    Clear definitions on what qualifies as sexual or adult content.

    Explicit guidelines on where this content is permitted (e.g., only in private or age-gated worlds).

    Explicit rules on whether ERP (erotic roleplay), kink behavior, or pornographic avatars/worlds are allowed at all, and in what contexts.

2. 🚨 NSFW Flagging System (Reddit-Style)

Introduce an NSFW tag system that includes:

    User-uploaded avatar warnings (checkbox for NSFW/mature content).

    World uploader tags to mark worlds as NSFW or 18+.

    Instance-level visibility settings to hide/show NSFW content depending on user preferences or age verification.

    Option for users to filter out or opt in to seeing flagged content (like Reddit’s NSFW content toggle).

This gives users full control over their content exposure and protects underage or uncomfortable users from stumbling into inappropriate environments.

⚖️ 3. Clarify Harassment vs Competitive Behavior (Employment Poaching)

There is a pressing need to distinguish between:

    Harassment: Targeted, repeated behavior aimed to harm, intimidate, or coerce users.

    Poaching Talent (Legal Competitive Practice): Reaching out to creators, developers, or staff in a non-hostile, non-coercive way to invite them to join another group or community.

I propose that VRChat:

    Define harassment clearly as intent to harm or intimidate, not simply recruiting someone from another project.

    Protect users from being falsely reported for "harassment" when engaging in standard industry or creative competition.

    Encourage community leaders to resolve disputes professionally, and ensure that ToS cannot be used to retaliate against competitive outreach.

This is crucial for fostering a healthy creator ecosystem where collaboration and fair competition are not discouraged.

💰 4. Guidelines for Monetized Moderation (Bag Checks, Fines, Paid Bans)

We are seeing rising use of monetized moderation models — particularly by groups like The Jungle — which include:

    Bag checks (charging individuals to "review" behavior).

    Fines for in-group behavioral infractions.

    Paid bans or third-party moderation-for-hire (groups accepting payment to ban a user across multiple servers or worlds).

Request:

    Add provisions to the ToS restricting or clearly outlining what is allowed when it comes to paid moderation services.

    Define whether it is acceptable for a group to charge users to avoid bans or be reinstated, especially if this is done under the threat of “network-wide punishment.”

    Ban or regulate pay-to-blacklist practices unless explicitly approved through platform governance.

This ensures no user can be extorted or blacklisted unjustly, and that group-based justice systems do not become exploitative.

5. 🛡️ NSFW Moderation Plan

Alongside ToS updates, I recommend VRChat publish a Moderation Plan that outlines common violations and corresponding actions. This helps set expectations and reduces confusion about bans or warnings in the future.

✅ Goals

    Clarifies boundaries and prevents misuse of moderation powers.

    Protects users from false harassment claims or unethical group practices.

    Prevents abuse of monetized systems (e.g. bag checks, pay-to-ban).

    Helps VRChat remain a creative-first, safe, and fair platform for all.

I am happy to help iterate on these suggestions and strongly believe this would benefit both the safety and creativity of the VRChat community.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best,

Night

Owner of Night Life
